chapter: Alfred Williams and the Ruidoso summer
title: Alfred sends for Watts in 1946
summary: Alfred, in New Orleans to marry off his daughter, asks to hire Watts for his El Paso band despite his reputation as a drinker.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: How long had you been home when I come down here in 46 to marry my daughter off? You see, you were here, you know?
Yeah. Well, I got out to home in 45. I'd just come back in 45. You said come back? Yeah, you see, I went overseas for a year and a half. That's right.
And I told H.E. I needed a trumpet player. Remember that?

And H.E. said, I'll get in touch with Bob. Yeah. I said, he'll go. I said, well, I'd like to have Bob, because, see, he been out there, and he would stay. You know? So, I want somebody to stay. Yeah. And I said, I know Bob, but they just say he's a bad actor, man. I'm telling you, he's a bad actor. Yeah. Oh, yeah. At that time, he's a bad actor. I was a fool was shorty, too, then. Yeah, fool was shorty. I said, I don't care. I'm going to give him a break. He's colored. I got Mexican, so I'm going to give him a break. Yeah. For all joy, thank you, Bob. Thank you.
